market_holds: Spot $334.19 at the 2026-11-19 seal (baseline), down 2.5% over 5 days and 2.2% over 20 days, 25% below the 52-week high of about $445 (2026-08-17 close $445.38) and 69% above the low. 20-day realised vol is 57% annualised, so an ordinary day moves about 3.6%. The option chain is thin (open interest 515, ATM spread 24% of mid) and gives no usable event premium, so the usual move is the median of 7 prior reactions, 6.0% (range -7.2% to +8.2%, 3 of 7 up). The last two fiscal-Q4/next-year-guide prints went +2.7% (2024-11-01, own Yahoo bars) and +8.2% (2025-11-21). Consensus as of mid-Nov: Q4 adjusted EPS $2.70 on $1.12bn (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-15) or $2.77-2.78 (Chartmill; FY26 consensus $11.77 less the $8.99 reported over 9 months); FY26 $11.77 from 5 analysts and FY27 $12.24 on $4.73bn (stockanalysis, checked 2026-11-10; last target changes 2026-10-09/13). Company guide FY26 adjusted EPS $11.65 +/- $0.10 (Q3 call 2026-07-31), so Q4 is implied at $2.56-2.76 and consensus already sits at or above the top of that range. The $11.65 includes about $0.70 of IEEPA tariff refund, so a clean base is about $10.95. FY27 consensus is +5% on the headline and +12% on the clean base. The drawdown since August belongs to the sector and the tape, not to Moog: from 2026-08-04 to 2026-11-19, MOG.A fell 18%, ITA 19%, CW 41% and HXL 26%. The -9.9% on 2026-11-04 came the same day as CW -9.2% and VRT -13%, and the -5.3% on 11-05 came with SPY -4.4%. Moog has had no own news since the 07-31 8-K (EDGAR submissions show only Form 4s, a 144 and 13G/As). The July print (-7.0%) came after a 30% three-month run-up, at a 43.6x P/E, with earnings flattered by one-offs. The preview's framing is that the FY27 guide must show growth without those one-offs. Short interest is unknown. A December Investor Day is pending.
view: The print turns on the FY27 guide set against the inflated FY26 base. The Q4 EPS line is second. Moog under its current CEO guides low and beats. Q4 FY25 'significantly exceeded the high end of our guidance range'. The Q1 FY26 guide was $2.20 +/- 0.10 and Moog reported $2.63. Q2 came in at $2.64 against a $2.38 consensus. The initial FY26 guide of $10.00 was described as above Street and drew +8.2%, and it has since been raised three times, to $10.95 even on a clean basis. The inputs to FY27 point to growth. Woodward guided FY27 sales +6-10% and EPS $10.20-10.70 on 2026-11-18 and rose about 5% today in a -1.2% tape; its commercial OEM sales grew 26% in Q4 on higher build rates. Airbus is weighing an A350 rate above 12/month and Boeing is aiming for 10/month on the 787. Data-centre pump capacity quadrupled in a year with 'more demand than supply'. Missile multi-year rates were expected in backlog within 3-6 months of September. The Army's FY27 request puts about $2.1bn into MV-75 against $350m in FY26, and the FY26 gap was backfilled. A guide of +12-15% on the clean base would give about $12.3-12.6 against the $12.24 consensus. The price has not been driven up into the print: it de-rated with the A&D and AI-capex baskets and carries no own-news run-up. So the setup leans up. But the lean is modest. The headline FY27 growth will look small against $11.65. A December Investor Day gives management a reason to keep the initial guide tight. Management called tariffs 'structural' for commercial aircraft, at about 200bp. And this is a 57%-vol name in a falling tape, scored at 13:00 ET.
unpriced: Possibly the guide-setting habit: since FY25, consensus has trailed Moog's actual guides and results each quarter, and the price has de-rated with the sector on no company news. But FY27 consensus ($12.24) already allows for clean-base growth of about 12%, so the gap is a lean rather than a demonstrated miss in the estimates.

recommendation.reason: Management has a consistent record of guiding low and beating. A peer just showed the market rewarding a double-digit FY27 supplier guide, and the stock has de-rated with its sector rather than on its own news, so the print leans up. But FY27 consensus already sits at a reasonable clean-base growth rate. Headline growth over the refund-inflated FY26 can read as weak, and a pending Investor Day may keep the guide conservative. That leaves the probability below the 65 needed to act.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An initial FY27 adjusted EPS guide at or below about $12.00, i.e. low single-digit headline growth with the one-off framing, would make the downside more likely. A guide of $12.50 or more would push the view toward a confident long.

self_critique: FY27 consensus of $12.24 already assumes about 12% clean growth, which is roughly what Moog guided last year. So the 'guides low' habit may already be in the estimates, and a typical Moog initial guide (+9% sales, a mid-teens EPS step on a clean base) may only meet it. The headline comparison with $11.65 will look like single-digit growth. Management has a reason to be cautious ahead of its December Investor Day. And the stock is a 57%-vol name in a falling market (SPY -6.6% from its high, AI-capex names weak), so the 13:00 ET mark could be set by the tape. The July case showed the market will sell a beat on earnings quality.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition helped most: it showed the drawdown is the sector's and the tape's, not Moog's. P4 kept me from reading the July drop as a cushion. P7's 65 threshold correctly held back a lean built on management habit rather than on dated counterparty evidence about the FY27 line itself. www.sec.gov was refused without a declared user agent, so Form 4 contents and the 8-K exhibits could not be read.
